meta.description: Reusable Quant V4 teaching principles for explanation design, review, and future maturity gates.

rules.title: Explanation first, formula later
rules.principle: Start with the meaning of the situation before presenting a formula.
do: Introduce formula only after the relationship is clear
avoid: Opening with a formula without context

rules.title: Concrete to abstract
rules.principle: Move from real quantities to symbolic representation only when needed.
do: Use the objects named in the stem
avoid: Generic x-y explanations when values are enough

rules.title: Multiplier before algebra
rules.principle: For change and growth topics, teach multiplier reasoning before equation manipulation.

rules.title: Preserve the base
rules.principle: Explicitly state the base on which a percentage, ratio share, or rate is applied.
do: Say whether percent is on CP, SP, principal, or changed value

rules.title: Use parts for ratios
rules.principle: Teach ratios as parts before converting to actual values.
avoid: Treating ratio terms as actual values without total

rules.title: Show unit discipline
rules.principle: Units should be aligned before arithmetic and repeated in the final answer.
do: Carry units into the final answer

rules.title: Flag the likely trap
rules.principle: When a known exam trap exists, name it briefly and correct it.
do: Mention the misconception in one sentence

rules.title: One reasoning move per line
rules.principle: Explanations should progress in small, auditable steps.
do: Use one calculation or inference per line

rules.title: Avoid variable-first explanations
rules.principle: Do not introduce variables before the learner understands the relationship.
do: Describe the relationship in words first
Introduce variables only when the unknown cannot be computed directly
avoid: Let x be... as the first line for every explanation

rules.title: Answer style must match the question
rules.principle: Return count, amount, ratio, percentage, or unit according to the ask, not only according to the calculation path.
do: Use canonical answer style IDs where available
avoid: Returning a percentage when the question asks for count
